narrativeReportMd:
# DocumentReference R4-to-R6 assessment

R6 keeps the same `DocumentReference` resource identity but introduces several local hard instance-breaking changes. The largest migration risks are the `context` backbone being replaced by a repeating reference, `content.format` becoming `content.profile.value[x]`, `authenticator` becoming `attester`, removal of `masterIdentifier` and `context.sourcePatientInfo`, and `relatesTo.code` changing from a primitive code to `CodeableConcept`.

The main migration pattern is a flatter and richer DocumentReference model. Several R4 `context.*` children moved to root fields, but `sourcePatientInfo` did not get a direct replacement. R6 also adds richer downgrade-risk metadata such as `basedOn`, `version`, `modality`, `bodyStructure`, `content.profile`, and structured attestation.

Inherited base-resource and datatype-only changes are intentionally excluded from `findings[]` and listed in scope/out-of-scope and follow-up dependencies.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `DocumentReference` is the same resource identity but has high-impact local structural breaks. Top concerns are context flattening/retyping, `content.format` replacement, `authenticator` replacement, removed identifier/source-patient fields, and `relatesTo.code` changing JSON type. Main uncertainty is the exact intended policy for terminology and narrative changes in the ballot build.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The dominant theme is flattening and richer semantics: nested R4 context data moved to root elements, format metadata became profile metadata, attestation became structured, relationship codes became CodeableConcepts, and R6 can represent more workflow, body, modality, and profile metadata than R4. Downgrade paths need extensions or policy decisions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local structural, cardinality, type, reference target, and CodeSystem differences because they come from the supplied local StructureDefinitions and terminology artifacts. Confidence is medium for exact terminology expansion differences and ballot-intent rationale because official diffs, rendered narrative pages, terminology-server expansions, and ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: R4 masterIdentifier was removed

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `masterIdentifier` as a 0..1 `Identifier` for the source-assigned, version-specific document identifier.

semanticText.definition: Document identifier as assigned by the source of the document; specific to this version of the document.

newState.summary: R6 has no `masterIdentifier`. `identifier` remains 0..* `Identifier`; `version` is a new optional `string`.

facts.note: Neither is a mandated lossless replacement for the old Identifier.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `identifier` is the nearest structural carrier and now maps to XDS uniqueId, while `version` cannot carry Identifier metadata such as system, type, assigner, or period.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `masterIdentifier` contain an element not defined in R6. Strict validators and generated R6 parsers can reject or drop it, and automatic migration can lose identifier metadata.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Document identifiers are often used for deduplication, XDS/CDA correlation, legal retrieval, and audit.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify document identity into business identifiers plus a content version string.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `masterIdentifier` as a deprecated base element while adding `identifier` and `version` guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of clarifying document identity is reasonable, but outright removal of a common version-specific Identifier is not clearly required. R4 already separated `masterIdentifier` from other `identifier` values, so preserving the old field as deprecated would mostly retain existing semantics while steering new implementations to the R6 model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `DocumentReference.masterIdentifier` at `0..1` as deprecated, define its relationship to `identifier` and `version`, and recommend the new fields for new content. The tradeoff is continued legacy identity ambiguity and a field that might persist indefinitely, but it would preserve R4-valid instances with low to moderate long-term cost.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a legacy identity slot that may linger and confuse identifier/version conventions, but the compatibility cost is manageable.

evidence.detail: No R6 element with this id exists.
R6 `identifier` maps to XDS entryUUID/uniqueId and CDA id; R6 `version` is a string.

examples.examplesMd: Illustrative fragments only; migration should preserve the Identifier metadata rather than blindly placing the value in `version`.

findings.narrativeMd: `masterIdentifier` is a concrete local removed element. It is not merely inherited or renamed; the closest R6 fields have different semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: any R4 instance with `masterIdentifier` has an unknown R6 element. R6-to-R4 is only an issue if an R4 client expects the former value to be reconstructed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `masterIdentifier` usage and define whether each value maps to `identifier`, `version`, both, or an extension. Test document lookup and duplicate detection after migration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated field or official slice would have been less disruptive but would preserve ambiguity between version-specific and general identifiers.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed because local identity conventions determine the correct target.

findings.title: authenticator Reference was replaced by structured attester

semanticText.definition: Which person or organization authenticates that this document is valid.

newState.summary: R6 has 0..* `attester`; each repetition requires `attester.mode` and may include `time` and `party`.

semanticText.definition: A participant who has authenticated the accuracy of the document.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old authenticator and new attester both map to document attestation/legal authenticator concepts.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `authenticator` is unknown in R6. Mapping it to `attester.party` is not enough because `attester.mode` is required when `attester` exists.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Authentication and attestation can carry legal provenance and trust implications.

justification.inferredGoal: Align DocumentReference with Composition-style attestation and support multiple attesters/modes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated `authenticator` shortcut while adding structured `attester`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting multiple attesters with explicit attestation mode is reasonable. A retained alias would preserve old JSON, but it would leave legal/professional attestation split between a simple reference and the richer backbone, requiring reconciliation rules and risking inconsistent trust semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `authenticator` as deprecated and mapped it to `attester.party` for migration. That only partially meets the goal because `attester.mode` is mandatory and semantically important; defaulting or inferring it in the base model would be unsafe, while allowing both fields would duplicate attestation indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Creates duplicate attestation representations, and the old shortcut lacks required mode/time semantics.

evidence.detail: R6 `party` carries the participant reference and includes the old target types plus Patient, RelatedPerson, and Group.

examples.examplesMd: The `mode` value must come from local provenance policy; it should not be silently guessed.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a local structural replacement from a simple reference to a repeatable attestation component.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for any R4 `authenticator`. R6-to-R4 cannot cleanly represent multiple attesters or attester parties outside the old target set.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `authenticator` to `attester.party` and define rules for `attester.mode`. Review legal/professional attestation semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Retaining a deprecated `authenticator` would have reduced validation breakage but left two representations of attestation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Manual review is recommended where attestation mode is not obvious from source data.

findings.title: content.format was replaced by content.profile.value[x]

newState.summary: R6 removes `content.format` and adds 0..* `content.profile`; each profile has required `value[x]` of Coding, uri, or canonical.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 `content.profile` has aliases including format/formatCode and maps to the same document format/profile role.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The path and JSON shape changed. R4 `content.format` is unknown in R6, and R6 URI/canonical profile values cannot be represented by R4 `Coding` without conversion or extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Format/profile metadata can determine safe rendering, parsing, and template validation.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent document formats, templates, and FHIR profiles more flexibly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `content.profile` while keeping deprecated `content.format` for Coding-valued formats.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of representing document constraints, templates, and FHIR profiles more flexibly is reasonable. Keeping `content.format` would reduce R4 validation breakage, but it would leave two same-resource carriers for overlapping format/profile facts and create conflict-handling obligations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep `content.format` as a deprecated Coding alias and add `content.profile` for the richer R6 cases. This would preserve old instances but only partially meet the R6 model: URI and canonical profiles still need the new field, and duplicate Coding values could diverge from `content.profile.valueCoding`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 Coding cases but duplicates format/profile metadata and cannot cover URI or canonical profile values.

evidence.detail: R6 defines required profile value choice Coding, uri, or canonical.
The binding target also changes from R4 `formatcodes` to v3-HL7FormatCodes.

findings.narrativeMd: Document format metadata moved from a single `Coding` field to repeatable profile metadata with a choice value.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for `content.format`. R6 `content.profile` is new-valid/old-invalid; URI and canonical values have no direct R4 base representation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old `format` to `profile.valueCoding`. Define downgrade handling for URI/canonical values, typically extension, local Coding, or rejection.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping `content.format` deprecated would have been less disruptive but would create duplicate format/profile representations.

findings.title: context changed from BackboneElement to repeating Reference

oldState.summary: R4 `context` was a 0..1 BackboneElement with children such as encounter, event, period, facilityType, practiceSetting, sourcePatientInfo, and related.

newState.summary: R6 `context` is 0..* Reference(Appointment|Encounter|EpisodeOfCare). Former children were flattened to root siblings, wrapped, or removed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The same path name now expects a different JSON shape: R4 used an object with children; R6 uses a list of Reference objects. Name-based migration is unsafe.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Encounter/context links can drive access control, clinical search, and workflow association.

justification.inferredGoal: Flatten clinical context and make workflow encounter context a direct reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a new encounter-context reference path and retain the old `context` backbone as deprecated.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Flattening clinical context and making encounter/workflow context a direct reference is a coherent R6 goal. The less-breaking path would have been technically possible, but retaining the old backbone alongside new root fields would duplicate many context facts and make validation and search semantics ambiguous.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have introduced a new reference element, such as an encounter-context field, while leaving the R4 `context` backbone valid but deprecated. That would preserve old instances, but implementers would then have to reconcile `context.encounter`, new encounter references, root `event`, root `period`, root `facilityType`, root `practiceSetting`, and related-resource fields, with a high risk that deprecated representations never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids same-name/different-type breakage but preserves a large duplicate context model that must be reconciled with root fields.

findings.narrativeMd: This is the central local context refactor. R4 `context` object data must be flattened; R6 `context` is specifically encounter/workflow context.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for any R4 `context` object. R6 Appointment context cannot be downgraded to R4 `context.encounter` without loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move R4 `context.encounter` references to root `context`; handle other children according to their specific findings. Update generated model code from component to reference list.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new path would have been safer for mixed-version clients but less tidy for the R6 model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because the path name is unchanged, automated diffs may understate this break.

findings.title: context.event moved to root event and changed to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 `context.event` was 0..* CodeableConcept with example v3-ActCode binding.

newState.summary: R6 root `event` is 0..* CodeableReference(Resource) with the same example concept binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The path moved and the JSON shape changed. Code-only R4 values can be wrapped as `event.concept`, but R6 reference-valued events have no R4 equivalent.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow events to be coded or linked to concrete resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `context.event` while adding root `event` as CodeableReference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing an event to be either a concept or a reference is a reasonable R6 goal. A deprecated old path would protect R4 instances, but it would only handle the concept side of the new model and would conflict with the broader context-flattening design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep `context.event` as a deprecated CodeableConcept list and add root `event` for CodeableReference. This preserves R4-coded events, but it leaves two event carriers in the same resource and still requires new representation for reference-valued events, so the alternative is incomplete and operationally messy.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old coded events but duplicates event representation and cannot represent R6 reference-valued events on the old path.

findings.narrativeMd: The event context is now a root CodeableReference, so implementers must change both path and generated type.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `context.event` is invalid in R6. R6 `event.reference` is not R4-representable unless converted to a code, extension, or related resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 values to `event.concept`; define a downgrade rule for R6 references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could be staged with an alias but would preserve the old context wrapper.

findings.title: context.related moved to related backbone with required target

newState.summary: R6 `related` is a 0..* BackboneElement with optional `code` and required `target` Reference(Resource).

impact.impactRationaleMd: A flat R4 reference list is invalid in R6. R6 `related.code` cannot be represented by the R4 base field.

justification.inferredGoal: Add relationship typing for non-lifecycle related resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Allow the old `context.related` reference list or a reference shorthand alongside `related.target`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding typed related-resource relationships is a reasonable goal. A compatibility shorthand would reduce parser breakage for old instances, but it would duplicate related-resource representation and leave the old form unable to carry the new relationship code.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `context.related` as deprecated or allowed `related` to accept a direct Reference shorthand. That would preserve simple R4 references, but systems would need rules for conflicts between shorthand references and `related.target`, and R6 `related.code` would remain unrepresentable in the old shape.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves simple R4 references but creates two relationship shapes and loses the R6 relationship code on the old shape.

evidence.detail: R6 requires `related.target` under a related backbone item.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 wraps related resources in a backbone so the relationship may be coded.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `context.related` is invalid in R6; R6 `related` is invalid in R4 unless projected back to `context.related` with loss of `code`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap each old reference as `related.target`; preserve R6 `related.code` in an extension when downgrading.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transitional shorthand would reduce parser breaks but duplicate representation.

findings.title: context.sourcePatientInfo was removed without a direct replacement

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `context.sourcePatientInfo` Reference(Patient) for patient information known when the document was published.

newState.summary: No direct R6 DocumentReference field carries the source patient information snapshot.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using this field contain a removed element, and mapping it to `subject` can be semantically wrong.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Source patient demographics at publication time can matter for provenance, patient matching, and legal audit.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify context and avoid duplicating patient subject data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the old `context.sourcePatientInfo` path as a deprecated base field during the context transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Simplifying context is reasonable, but removing source-patient snapshot information without a base replacement appears avoidable. The field is not semantically equivalent to `subject`, and an extension or profile workaround would be only a migration mitigation, not a backwards-compatible base R6 design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `DocumentReference.context.sourcePatientInfo` as deprecated as part of a transitional context backbone, with clear guidance that new R6 content should use a more explicit provenance pattern if one is standardized. This would preserve R4-valid instances and important historical-demographic semantics at modest cost.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a narrow legacy provenance field and some context-refactor baggage, but avoids losing source-patient snapshot data.

evidence.detail: No R6 element with this id exists.

findings.narrativeMd: Unlike most context children, `sourcePatientInfo` did not reappear as a root sibling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for resources using this field. No base R6 field has the same meaning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not automatically map to `subject`. Preserve in an extension, Provenance, contained Patient, or IG-specific profile if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An official extension or deprecated field would have preserved data without complicating common cases.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is important where source demographics differ from current Patient demographics.

findings.title: relatesTo.code changed from primitive code to CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 `relatesTo.code` was required primitive `code` with required binding to replaces, transforms, signs, appends.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local complete CodeSystem contains replaces, transforms, signs, appends.

newState.summary: R6 `relatesTo.code` is required `CodeableConcept` with extensible binding; the CodeSystem adds incorporates and summarizes.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Compared local complete CodeSystem resources; no terminology-server expansion was run.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON value changes from a primitive string to an object. R6-only codes, multiple codings, and text-only concepts cannot be downgraded to the R4 required primitive enum without policy mapping.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lifecycle relationship codes affect supersession, appendices, signatures, summaries, and transformed documents.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer relationship coding and additional relationship semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the primitive code as a deprecated alias or add a separate CodeableConcept relationship field.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Richer relationship coding and additional lifecycle semantics are reasonable R6 goals. The old primitive code could be preserved for compatibility, but doing so would split a safety-relevant lifecycle fact between primitive and CodeableConcept representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep `relatesTo.code` as the primitive required code and add a new optional CodeableConcept field, or retain the primitive as a deprecated alias. That would preserve R4 instances but only partially meet the R6 goal because multiple codings, text, and extensible terminology semantics would still require the new representation, with conflict rules for duplicate fields.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces primitive-string breakage but duplicates lifecycle relationship representation and cannot fully support richer codings on the old field.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `incorporates` and `summarizes`; old codes are retained.

findings.narrativeMd: `relatesTo.code` is a hard codegen break and a lifecycle terminology change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 primitive strings are invalid R6 until wrapped as CodeableConcept. R6 codes outside the old four-code set are invalid in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old values in a Coding with the HL7 relationship system. Update enum switches and define downgrade mappings for `incorporates` and `summarizes`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An alias would reduce breakage but conflicts with FHIR's normal single representation for coded concepts.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Lifecycle semantics are business-sensitive; avoid collapsing all new codes into a generic relation.

findings.title: date widened from instant to dateTime

newState.summary: R6 `date` is 0..1 `dateTime` and asks producers to provide the most precise timestamp available.

semanticText.comment: Provide the most precise timestamp available.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instants are valid R6 dateTimes, so old instances should remain valid. R6 can use reduced-precision dateTimes that cannot be represented as R4 instant without inventing precision/timezone.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow indexing/reference dates when a full instant is unavailable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because R4 `instant` values remain valid R6 `dateTime` values.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing less precise dates when an exact instant is unavailable is a reasonable R6 goal, and the type widening should not invalidate R4 instances. The main compatibility risk is that new reduced-precision R6 values cannot be served back to R4 as `instant` without a lossy policy.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is a widening for R4-to-R6 validation, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Keeping `instant` or adding a separate approximate date field would preserve R4 downgrade behavior but would sacrifice or split the R6 capture/search model rather than avoid an R4-to-R6 break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 precision downgrade, not preservation of old R4 instances.

examples.examplesMd: Month-level R6 dateTime cannot be converted to an R4 instant without a lossy convention.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 hard break but affects runtime assumptions about precision.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instants remain syntactically valid. R6 partial dateTimes are new-valid/old-invalid.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Copy R4 instants forward. For downgrade, reject partial precision, preserve it in an extension, or apply a documented normalization rule.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new approximate date element would have preserved compatibility but split search semantics.

findings.title: subject and author reference targets were widened

oldState.summary: R4 subject targets Patient, Practitioner, Group, Device; author targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Device, Patient, RelatedPerson.

newState.summary: R6 subject targets any Resource; author adds CareTeam and Group.

impact.impactRationaleMd: All R4 targets remain allowed, but R6 can legally reference resource types that R4 validators reject.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow documents about and authored by a wider range of resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening the types of resources that can be document subjects or authors is a reasonable expressive change. Since R4-valid target types remain valid in R6, this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The only way to avoid the R6-to-R4 downgrade gap would be to keep the R4 target lists, which would block the R6 expressiveness goal. That is not a backwards-compatible alternative for preserving old R4 instances because those instances are already preserved.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: All R4 targets remain allowed; the tradeoff is only that some R6 targets cannot validate in R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the reference target sets were widened.

evidence.detail: R6 subject targets Resource and author includes CareTeam and Group.

findings.narrativeMd: Reference target widening is forward-compatible but creates R6-to-R4 validation gaps.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances remain valid for target profiles. R6 values outside the R4 sets are not R4-representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Detect unsupported target types before downgrade and preserve them using extensions or profile-specific rules.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The only fully compatible alternative would avoid the useful R6 widening.

findings.title: docStatus required code system expanded and semantics refined

oldState.summary: R4 `docStatus` was required-bound to composition-status with preliminary, final, amended, entered-in-error.

newState.summary: R6 keeps required binding but adds registered, partial, corrected, appended, cancelled, deprecated, and unknown; preliminary is semantically refined.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: Content may be incomplete or unverified.
changedCodes.newMeaning: Verified early results are available, but not all results are final.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Definition refined under the new partial hierarchy.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old codes are retained, so R4 instances remain code-valid. R6-only required-binding codes cannot be represented in R4 without lossy mapping, and `preliminary` semantics changed.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Document status can affect clinical use, finality, correction handling, and deprecation.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent a more granular document lifecycle.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep existing code meanings, especially `preliminary`, and add new codes for narrower lifecycle distinctions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A more granular document lifecycle code system is reasonable, but narrowing the semantics of an existing R4 code is not clearly justified by the local evidence. Existing `preliminary` instances can remain code-valid while being interpreted differently, which is the kind of semantic break that could have been avoided by adding new codes rather than redefining the old one.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could preserve the R4 meaning of `preliminary` and add separate R6 codes for the newly distinguished states, such as verified early results or broader partial availability. This keeps old data semantics stable with only moderate terminology complexity; ConceptMaps help migration but are not a base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds or retains more lifecycle codes and still needs downgrade policy, but avoids changing the meaning of legacy data.

evidence.detail: R6 adds seven composition-status codes while retaining old codes.

findings.narrativeMd: `docStatus` keeps the same primitive field but its required terminology is materially broader and semantically refined.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation should pass for old codes. R6-to-R4 fails for new codes unless mapped or extended.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update enums and status logic. Define clinically approved downgrade mappings for new statuses rather than silently collapsing them.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An official ConceptMap would mitigate the otherwise unavoidable semantic downgrade problem.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for lossy lifecycle-status mappings.

findings.title: content repetition semantics were tightened

oldState.summary: R4 allowed multiple content repetitions, described as different formats.

newState.summary: R6 says multiple content repetitions must represent the same document in different format or attachment metadata and must not contain different versions.

semanticText.comment: content element shall not contain different versions of the same content. For version handling use multiple DocumentReference with .relatesTo.

facts.oldValue: Multiple content repetitions each with a different format.
facts.newValue: Repetitions must represent the same document and not different versions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No local error invariant enforces this, so base validators may not reject old instances. It is still a conformance break for systems that used content repetitions for different versions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mixing alternate formats with different versions can cause consumers to display or rely on stale content.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify document identity and use `relatesTo` for versioning.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep permissive R4 repetition semantics and add advisory guidance or profile warnings for version packing.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of preventing different document versions from being hidden inside one `DocumentReference.content` list is clinically and operationally reasonable. A softer advisory path would be less disruptive, but it would not give base R6 consumers a reliable same-document invariant.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could leave the R4 semantics intact and add best-practice guidance, a warning, or a profile recommendation to use separate DocumentReferences with `relatesTo` for versions. That is only a partial alternative because systems could still legitimately pack multiple versions in the base resource, undermining the interoperability and safety goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old multi-version packing patterns but weakens the R6 guarantee that repetitions are alternate forms of the same document.

evidence.detail: R4 says multiple repetitions may each have a different format.
R6 says repetitions must represent the same document and not different versions.

examples.examplesMd: This pattern is problematic if the two attachments are versions rather than alternate formats of the same document.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 narrows the intended meaning of repeated `content` without changing cardinality.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Still-valid-but-behaviorally-different unless profiles or validators enforce narrative conformance. Some old usages may become nonconformant.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit multi-content resources. Split different versions into separate DocumentReferences connected with `relatesTo`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning invariant would have made the migration signal clearer and more toolable.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed where content URLs/hashes suggest different document versions.

findings.title: R6 adds warning constraints involving facilityType, practiceSetting, and Encounter context

oldState.summary: R4 had no local docRef-1/docRef-2 constraints.

newState.summary: R6 adds warning constraints docRef-1 and docRef-2.

constraints.human: facilityType SHALL only be present if context is not an encounter
practiceSetting SHALL only be present if context is not present

impact.impactRationaleMd: The constraints are warnings, so most validators should not fail instances, but warning-as-error pipelines or conformance review may flag migrated resources with Encounter context plus facility/practice metadata.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid duplicating facility/practice metadata that can be derived from Encounter.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use clearer SHOULD/best-practice guidance or profile-level warnings instead of base SHALL warning constraints.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Avoiding duplicate facility/practice metadata when an Encounter supplies it is a plausible R6 goal, and warning severity keeps the normal validation break limited. The main concern is the mismatch between SHALL wording and warning behavior, so a less-breaking alternative exists but would reduce toolable conformance pressure.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could phrase the rule as SHOULD/best-practice narrative or leave enforcement to profiles that know whether Encounter-derived metadata is reliable. That would reduce migration uncertainty for R4 data but only partially meet the R6 goal because base validators would have less consistent ability to flag duplicated context metadata.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids warning-as-error ambiguity but gives validators and reviewers a weaker, less uniform signal.

evidence.detail: R6 adds a warning when facilityType is present with Encounter context.
R6 adds a warning when practiceSetting is present with Encounter context.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is structurally R6-shaped but can trigger warning constraints if `context` resolves to Encounter.

findings.narrativeMd: The constraints interact with the context flattening and may affect validation quality gates.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Potential break only where warnings are treated as failures or SHALL wording is enforced strictly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When moving R4 `context.facilityType` and `context.practiceSetting` to root, check whether Encounter already conveys those concepts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same rule could be introduced as clearer best-practice guidance to reduce ambiguity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The docRef-2 human text says context not present, while the expression tests no Encounter in context; verify intended ballot wording.

findings.title: securityLabel binding weakened and semantics clarified

newState.summary: R6 has example binding to `security-label-example` and clarifies labels apply to the referenced document, while `meta.security` applies to DocumentReference metadata.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old instances remain structurally valid, but terminology validation is weaker and security policy engines may need to distinguish document-content labels from metadata labels.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Security-label interpretation can affect access control and privacy handling.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify document-content security classification separately from metadata security.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because weakening the binding does not invalidate R4 security labels.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that `securityLabel` applies to the referenced document while `meta.security` applies to metadata is a reasonable R6 goal. The binding-strength decrease may affect policy expectations, but it does not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Retaining the R4 extensible binding while updating the definition would have preserved stronger terminology guidance, but this is not a backwards-compatible base-design alternative in the R4-to-R6 instance sense: old codes remain allowed under the weaker example binding. The remaining risk is policy/runtime interpretation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the extensible binding could improve uniform policy guidance, but that is conformance strictness rather than R4 instance preservation.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is extensible to security-labels.
R6 binding is example and definition distinguishes document labels from `meta.security` metadata labels.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON shape changes are needed; the risk is validation and policy interpretation.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not a hard instance break, but it is material for security policy and conformance.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base R6 validation is less restrictive than R4 terminology guidance. Runtime policy behavior may change even when JSON is valid.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review access-control logic. Put metadata-level labels in `meta.security` and underlying document labels in `securityLabel`; keep local value-set validation if required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6 could have preserved the extensible binding while clarifying semantics, but may have intended more flexibility for document-content labels.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Full value-set expansion was not performed.

findings.title: status short text mentions unknown but required value set does not

oldState.summary: R4 status short text and required CodeSystem list current, superseded, entered-in-error.

newState.summary: R6 status short text lists unknown, but the local R6 CodeSystem/ValueSet still contains only current, superseded, entered-in-error.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Do not treat `unknown` as valid based only on the short text. Binding-aware validators should reject it, but generated documentation or UI picklists may be wrong.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: This is not a confirmed R4-to-R6 base compatibility issue; R4 did not allow `unknown`, and the R6 required ValueSet still does not.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local R6 artifacts conflict: the short text mentions `unknown`, but the required terminology artifacts still list only the R4 codes. Without ballot notes or a later package, the intended goal cannot be assessed, and no R4-valid status value is shown to become invalid.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The compatible fix is to align the short text with the required ValueSet if `unknown` was accidental. If R6 intended to add `unknown`, that would be an R6-to-R4 expansion concern rather than a less-breaking alternative for preserving R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Correcting the short text is compatible; adding `unknown` would create a new R6-to-R4 downgrade issue.

evidence.detail: Local R6 terminology still has only current, superseded, entered-in-error.

examples.examplesMd: This fragment illustrates the inconsistency; based on the local required binding, it should not validate.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a ballot inconsistency rather than a confirmed status code addition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Binding-aware R6 validators should reject `unknown`; non-binding-aware generators might accept it and later fail validation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Generate status enums and validators from the required ValueSet/CodeSystem, not the short text. Re-check in a later R6 build.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The compatible fix is editorial unless R6 intended a real code addition.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Verify against official ballot notes or later package versions.

findings.title: type and category binding value sets changed

oldState.summary: R4 type preferred binding was `c80-doc-typecodes`; category example binding was `document-classcodes`.

newState.summary: R6 type preferred binding is `doc-typecodes`; category example binding is `referenced-item-category`, combining media-category and LOINC DOC-scale guidance.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Binding strengths remain preferred/example, so base validation should not reject old codes. The change can still affect picklists, analytics, and profiles that copied core value sets.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Modernizing terminology guidance for document type and category is reasonable, and the retained non-required binding strengths avoid a hard R4-to-R6 validation break. The migration work is mainly in UIs, analytics, and profiles that copied the old guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because preferred and example binding changes do not make old base instances invalid, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Implementations that need the old value sets can retain them in profiles or local configuration, but that is not a less-breaking base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Old picklists and profiles may need local retention, but base validation does not reject old codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the bindings remain preferred/example.

evidence.detail: R6 referenced-item-category includes media-category and LOINC DOC-scale criteria.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON shape change; effect is terminology guidance and downstream profiling.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a material semantic/conformance guidance change, not a hard base validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Preferred/example bindings should not make old instances invalid, but strengthened profiles may need updates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review UI picklists, analytic groupers, and IG bindings for `type` and `category`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Non-required binding changes are intentionally lower-risk; old terminology can remain in profiles if needed.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Full LOINC/filter expansions were not compared.

findings.title: New optional R6 metadata is not directly representable in R4

affectedLocation.newPath: DocumentReference.version / basedOn / modality / bodyStructure / period / facilityType / practiceSetting / related / attester / content.profile

oldState.summary: R4 lacks several R6 fields or only has less expressive/nested predecessors.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional metadata including `version`, `basedOn`, `modality`, `bodyStructure`, root `period`, root `facilityType`, root `practiceSetting`, `related`, `attester`, and `content.profile`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are optional and do not invalidate R4 instances moving forward, but R6 instances that use them lose information or require extensions when served to R4 clients.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropped workflow, attestation, body-site, modality, or profile metadata can affect routing, imaging interpretation, and trust decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Add metadata missing or under-modeled in R4 DocumentReference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the grouped R6 fields are optional additions or downgrade-only concerns.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional metadata for workflow, modality, body structure, attestation, relationships, and profiles is a reasonable R6 goal and does not invalidate R4 instances moving forward. The identified risk is R6-to-R4 representability, not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Cross-version extensions or projections can mitigate R6-to-R4 loss, but they are downgrade mechanisms rather than base-design alternatives. Since the fields are optional additions, the backwards-compatible R4-to-R6 alternative question is not applicable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 downgrade and round-trip fidelity still require policy, but avoiding the fields would block useful R6 expressiveness.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds substantial optional metadata. It is not a forward break, but it is a round-trip and downgrade risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 can omit the new fields. R6-to-R4 must drop, extension-preserve, or project them into narrower R4 fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define downgrade extensions for locally used R6 fields and avoid silent data loss in R4 APIs or stores.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Additive optional fields are the least disruptive forward path, but they cannot be fully backward-compatible with R4.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This grouped finding is for downgrade planning; dedicated findings cover the largest individual reshaped elements.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag remain aligned. R6 exists as a direct counterpart.

No retained common element was found with a local minimum cardinality increase. Required `status` remains 1..1 and `content` remains 1..*. Required children under new optional backbones are covered in findings.
`relatesTo.target` remains Reference(DocumentReference). Subject and author target sets widened, not narrowed, and are covered as downgrade risk.
No local DocumentReference element newly became a modifier. `status` remains modifier=true.
No material slicing change was found on base DocumentReference elements.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value additions/removals were found.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were found for DocumentReference elements.
Material binding changes are reported. No external terminology-server expansions were run for filter-based or external value sets.
`identifier`, `status`, `docStatus`, `content.attachment`, and `relatesTo.target` retained their core datatypes; material type replacements are findings.
